stem.text: Let \( f(x) = \begin{cases} \frac{x^{2} - 9}{x + 3}, & x < -3 \\ kx + m, & -3 \le x \le -1 \\ 3 x^{2} + 9, & x > -1 \end{cases} \), where k and m are constants. Find the values of k and m for which f is continuous for all real numbers. Show that the function value at each boundary agrees with both one sided limits.

answer_key.label: \( k = 9 \) and \( m = 21 \), because the middle branch must equal -6 at \( x = -3 \) and 12 at \( x = -1 \).

worked_solution.text: For \( x < -3 \), \( \frac{x^{2} - 9}{x + 3} = x - 3 \), so the limit from the left at \( x = -3 \) is -6. The middle branch gives \( f(-3) = -3k + m \), so \( -3k + m = -6 \).
worked_solution.rule_named: match the branches at the first boundary

worked_solution.text: At \( x = -1 \) the middle branch gives \( f(-1) = -1k + m \) and the last branch approaches 12, so \( -1k + m = 12 \).
worked_solution.rule_named: match the branches at the second boundary

worked_solution.text: Subtracting the equations gives \( k = 9 \), and then \( m = 21 \).

options.label: \( k = 9 \) and \( m = 21 \), because the middle branch must equal -6 at \( x = -3 \) and 12 at \( x = -1 \).
No values of k and m work, because \( \frac{x^{2} - 9}{x + 3} \) is undefined at \( x = -3 \), so f has no limit there.
options.derivation: the first branch is undefined at x = -3, and that was taken to mean its limit there does not exist

options.label: \( k = -12 \) and \( m = 0 \), because the middle branch must equal 36 at \( x = -3 \) and 12 at \( x = -1 \).
options.derivation: at x = -3 the last branch, which applies only for x > -1, used in place of the first branch

options.derivation: at x = -1 the first branch, which applies only for x < -3, used in place of the last branch
